_comment: CFD product specs. Same format and same builder as data/futures-specs.json —
`npm run db:cfd` expands it into import rows.
Every product here is `uncertain` on purpose. The firm and product NAMES come
from an aggregator export, which is a legitimate use of one: discovery. Its
FIGURES are not usable — 18 of its 28 CFD rows shared byte-identical price,
drawdown, split and payout values, which is a filled-down column rather than a
market. So no figure was carried across.
To fill this in, supply per-size figures per product exactly as the futures
data was supplied: sizes, profit target, max drawdown, daily loss limit,
drawdown type, consistency, minimum days, profit split and price. CFD firms
usually publish percentages rather than dollars — use `target_pct`, `dd_pct`
and `daily_pct` at product level for those, and `sizes` for anything that
`phases` is worth care here: CFD firms commonly run 2-step evaluations, which
futures firms rarely do. Set `program` to `evaluation` and record the phase
count in `notes` until a phases field is added.
